title: Berlin to Prague by Train: The Ultimate Travel Guide (2026)
short: Berlin to Prague by direct train, with tickets, track works, border rules and alternatives.
summary: Direct Berlin trains run from Berlin Hauptbahnhof to Praha hlavni nadrazi in about 4 hours, with 7 to 8 trains a day each way and advance fares from about 18 EUR one way. This guide covers fares, seat reservations, the Monday and daytime track closures near the border, luggage, border checks and the options by bus, plane and car.

blocks.text: The direct Berlin trains are modern Czech ComfortJet trains run by Ceske drahy (Czech Railways) with Deutsche Bahn. They run from Berlin through Dresden, Bad Schandau, Decin and Usti nad Labem to Prague, and follow the Elbe and then the Vltava valley. Both countries are in the Schengen area, so there is no border stop and no passport queue on the train.

No routine checks. Germany has temporary controls at its Czech border, so police spot checks on trains are possible. Carry a passport or ID card.

blocks.text: Mondays are different. Until autumn 2027 the Elbe valley line near the border is closed on Mondays from about 09:00 to 19:00, and most trains are cancelled or replaced by buses. Plan around the early and evening trains or travel on another day. Details are in the timetable section.

You can buy the same train from Deutsche Bahn (bahn.de or the DB Navigator app) or from Ceske drahy (cd.cz or the Muj vlak app). Seat61 reports that the two sites can show different prices for the same train, so compare both. Tickets go on sale up to 6 months ahead.

blocks.text: Ceske drahy advertises Prague to Berlin fares from 423 CZK and says it is cheaper to buy earlier. Fares change with the date and how full the train is. Cheap fares sell out first, so book as early as your plans allow, and check the date you want.

items: BahnCard 25, 50 and 100 give 25 percent off the German part of a Sparpreis Europa journey.

Children under 6 travel free. Children aged 6 to 14 can travel free with an adult on a Sparpreis fare if they are added to the booking, up to 4 children per ticket. Seat61 reports this must be added through Deutsche Bahn, not through cd.cz.
Deutsche Bahn's page gives different ages for the accompanying adult in different places, so read the conditions at booking.

Seat reservations: Deutsche Bahn charges 5.50 EUR in 2nd class and 6.90 EUR in 1st class, according to Seat61. Ceske drahy says a seat reservation can be free when you buy on cd.cz or in the Muj vlak app, and Interrail lists 3 EUR for the Czech section. On cd.cz you can pick a seat from a map.
Seat61 reports reservations are compulsory from mid-June to late August and strongly advised at other times. Check the operator's site for your date.

A Sparpreis ticket is tied to your booked train. If Deutsche Bahn expects a delay of 60 minutes or more at the destination on an international trip, the train binding is lifted and you can take a later train.

blocks.text: Interrail and Eurail pass holders: Interrail says Berlin to Prague reservations are not mandatory, but they are recommended. It lists 5.50 EUR in 2nd class and 6.90 EUR in 1st class on the German side and 3 EUR on the Czech side. Booking through the Interrail reservation system adds 2 EUR per person per train. The fees are indicative, so check the current amount.

Delay compensation: under EU rail passenger rights you can claim 25 percent of the ticket price for a delay of 60 to 119 minutes and 50 percent for 120 minutes or more. If the delay makes the trip pointless or the alternative would arrive more than 60 minutes late, you can claim a full refund. Claims for delays must be made within 3 months.

blocks.text: Mondays: the Elbe valley line between Bad Schandau and Schoena is closed every Monday from 09:00 to 19:00, except public holidays, from 23 March 2026 until November 2027, according to Deutsche Bahn. Seat61 says that on these Mondays, until 16 October 2027, most Berlin to Prague trains are cancelled. Only the early morning and evening trains run, and Seat61 lists the 06:23, 17:28 and 19:28 from Berlin.

Other daytime closures: the Elbe Cycle Route site lists further closures between Bad Schandau and Schoena from 09:10 to 17:10 on Tuesday 10 November to Friday 13 November 2026 and on Tuesday 1 December 2026. During closures the long-distance trains are cancelled or replaced by buses towards Usti nad Labem. Bicycles are often not carried on the buses.

Ceske drahy publishes diversion and closure notices for international trains, including work around the Berlin junction, on its foreign closures page. Check it and the DB Navigator app before you travel.
Peak days: Fridays, Sundays and holiday periods are the busiest. Reserve a seat in summer, when reservations are compulsory according to Seat61.
A day trip is possible. The 07:28 from Berlin reaches Praha hl. n. at 11:25 and the 16:31 from Prague reaches Berlin Hbf at 20:29. Avoid Mondays and the closure days listed above.

Berlin Hauptbahnhof sits close to the government district. Trains to Prague use the lower level, platforms 1 to 8 (level -2). S-Bahn trains leave from the upper platforms 15 and 16. The ticket office is on level +1, and the DB Information Point is open 24 hours. The DB Travel Center is open from 08:00 to 21:00 daily.

Luggage storage in Berlin: the Gepaeck Center on level +1 has lockers and a staffed left luggage office, according to Seat61. The berlin.de station page lists lockers in the car park outside the main building.

Praha hlavni nadrazi is at Wilsonova 8, Prague 2, near Wenceslas Square. The station has its own Metro line C stop and tram lines 5, 9, 15 and 26 nearby. Passenger areas are open daily from 03:30 to 01:15. Lockers are on level -2, and a staffed luggage office is on level -1. There are ticket counters, a taxi rank, a cash machine and an exchange office.

items: Train type: nine-car ComfortJet trains with two 1st class cars, six 2nd class cars and a restaurant car, according to Seat61.
Power and Wi-Fi: power sockets at all seats in both classes and free Wi-Fi. Seat61 says Wi-Fi is unlimited in the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Hungary and may be limited in Germany.

Food and drink: the restaurant car is open to everyone and serves meals at tables, plus snacks and drinks to take to your seat. In 1st class a steward takes orders at your seat. Take some cash in EUR or CZK as card machines can fail without mobile signal.

Luggage: Deutsche Bahn sets no weight limit and says you do not need to measure or weigh bags. Its standard rack size is 70 x 50 x 30 cm. You can bring hand luggage plus one larger piece free of charge, and up to three easily carried pieces on international trips. Large suitcases go in the luggage racks, and rolling cases should be laid down so they cannot roll.

Bikes: a bicycle space reservation is required. Deutsche Bahn says cross-border bike bookings may need a DB Travel Centre or the phone line +49 30 2970 (press 9 for English). Ceske drahy lists bicycle fees of 40 CZK for 1 to 150 km and 60 CZK for 151 km or more as accompanied luggage, with reservations free when bought with a ticket. Folding bikes travel free as hand luggage if stowed safely.
Prams, wheelchairs and walking aids travel free. Space can be limited at busy times.
Pets: check the Ceske drahy and Deutsche Bahn websites for the rules and fee for your animal before you travel.
Accessibility: contact Deutsche Bahn or Ceske drahy before travel to arrange help. Ceske drahy connection information is available around the clock on +420 221 111 122.

sections.title: Passports, border checks and entry rules

blocks.text: Status as of 11 November 2026. This is practical information only and not legal advice. Check the official pages before you travel.

Germany and the Czech Republic are both in the Schengen area, so there are no routine passport checks and no customs stop on the train. Germany has temporary internal border controls at all its land borders, including the Czech border. The Federal Police carry out spot checks on roads and trains, so be ready to show a valid passport or ID card on request. The ID requirement applies to rail travellers as well as drivers, according to ADAC. The Czech side has no systematic checks.

head: Rule
Status and date
rows: Germany has extended its controls beyond 15 September 2026. Media reports from August 2026 say the extension runs to about 15 March 2027, and ADAC describes the same plan. Controls at the Czech border have been in place since October 2023.
A valid passport or national ID card. Children travelling abroad need their own documents.
Visa-free visitors can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area

These apply to checks at the outer edge of the Schengen area, not to the Germany to Czech Republic crossing. Check the EU's official pages for the latest start dates before you fly in from outside Europe.
Visa rules depend on your nationality. If you need a Schengen visa, it covers both countries.

blocks.text: Currency: the Czech Republic uses the Czech koruna (CZK), not the euro. Some places in Prague accept euros but the rate is usually poor, so pay by card or withdraw koruna.

sections.title: Other ways to get from Berlin to Prague

blocks.text: Bus: FlixBus runs about 35 to 36 services a day on the route, according to its site, and lists a trip time of about 4 hours 20 minutes. Omio shows direct buses of about 4 to 5 hours 30 minutes. Fares start around 12 to 19 EUR or GBP and rise on busy dates. Berlin stops include the central bus station (Masurenallee), Suedkreuz, Alexanderplatz and the Central Station (Invalidenstrasse). In Prague, Florenc Central Bus Station is the main stop. FlixBus says its Main Railway Station stop moves to Opletalova Street from 3 August 2026. Luggage is one carry-on up to 7 kg and one checked bag up to 20 kg.

Flight: Skyscanner reports no direct flights from Berlin Brandenburg to Prague. Fares with a stop start from about 46 EUR one way, with Ryanair, Wizz Air and easyJet among the carriers. Rome2Rio gives about 6 hours door to door and a price range of 100 to 293 USD. With airport transfers, security and a connection, the train is faster and simpler.

Drive: the road distance is about 340 km and the drive takes about 3 hours 20 minutes in good traffic. Rome2Rio estimates about 71 to 102 USD in running costs. Czech motorways need an electronic vignette. For a standard car it costs 230 CZK for 1 day, 300 CZK for 10 days, 480 CZK for 30 days and 2,570 CZK for a year, according to Czech Post. Buy online at the official edalnice site, at a Czech Post office or at a petrol station near the border. Expect possible queues at German border checks, for example at Breitenau-Schoenwald, where ADAC reports increased checks and occasional jams.
Rideshare: Rome2Rio lists rideshare as the cheapest option at about 4 hours and roughly 18 to 23 USD. Use an established app and check the driver's reviews.

Other train operators: Leo Express serves Frankfurt, Dresden, Erfurt, Leipzig, Weimar and Prague but not Berlin, and it has said it will suspend its Dresden to Prague service from 5 October 2026 for the rest of the year. Use the Berlin ComfortJet trains for a direct journey.

faq.q: How long does the Berlin to Prague train take?
faq.a: The fastest direct train takes 3 hours 57 minutes to Praha hlavni nadrazi. Some trains take a few minutes longer.

faq.q: How many trains run from Berlin to Prague each day?
faq.a: There are 7 southbound trains from Berlin until 12 December 2026, about every two hours, and 8 from 13 December 2026. Fewer run on Mondays because of track work near the border.

faq.q: How much does the train from Berlin to Prague cost?
faq.a: Advance Sparpreis fares start from about 18 EUR in 2nd class and about 30 EUR in 1st class. Flexpreis fares are about 80 to 95 EUR in 2nd class and 138 to 160 EUR in 1st class. Prices change by date.

faq.q: Do I need a seat reservation?
faq.a: Usually it is optional but advised. Seat61 reports that reservations are compulsory from mid-June to late August. A reservation costs 5.50 EUR in 2nd class through Deutsche Bahn, and can be free or about 3 EUR through Ceske drahy.

faq.q: Why are there fewer trains on Mondays?
faq.a: The Elbe valley line between Bad Schandau and Schoena is closed on Mondays from about 09:00 to 19:00 until autumn 2027. Most trains are cancelled or replaced by buses. Only early and evening trains run.

faq.q: Do I need a passport to travel from Berlin to Prague?
faq.a: Yes, carry a passport or national ID card. There are no routine checks, but Germany has temporary controls at its Czech border, and police spot checks on trains are possible.

faq.q: What are the luggage limits?
faq.a: There is no weight limit. Deutsche Bahn allows hand luggage plus one larger piece free of charge, and up to three easily carried pieces on international trips. You must be able to carry each piece yourself.

faq.q: Can I take a bike on the train?
faq.a: Yes, with a bicycle space reservation. Deutsche Bahn says cross-border bike bookings may need a DB Travel Centre or its phone line. Bikes are often not carried on the replacement buses used during closures.

faq.q: Can children travel free?
faq.a: Children under 6 travel free. Children aged 6 to 14 can travel free with an adult on a Sparpreis fare if they are added to the booking.

faq.q: What if the train is delayed?
faq.a: For a delay of 60 to 119 minutes you can claim 25 percent of the ticket price. For 120 minutes or more you can claim 50 percent. You can also ask for a refund or re-routing if the delay is long.

faq.q: Is the train better than the bus?
faq.a: For most people, yes. The train is about as fast or faster, runs from centre to centre and has a restaurant car. The bus can be cheaper, especially on dates when cheap train fares are gone.

title: Brussels to Amsterdam by Train: Eurostar and Eurocity Direct Guide (2026)
short: Brussels to Amsterdam by train: two direct options, stations, tickets, border checks and what to do in Amsterdam.
summary: Two direct trains link Brussels and Amsterdam. Eurostar takes about 1 hour 50 minutes and arrives at Amsterdam Centraal. Eurocity Direct runs every hour, takes about 2 hours and arrives at Amsterdam Zuid, with fares from about 25 EUR. This guide explains which to choose, how to buy tickets, what to know at the border, and what to do in Amsterdam.

blocks.text: Two direct trains run between Brussels and Amsterdam. Eurostar is the faster one and ends at Amsterdam Centraal, in the middle of the city. Eurocity Direct (run by NS and SNCB) leaves every hour, is often cheaper, and ends at Amsterdam Zuid, a business district south of the centre. Both start at Brussels-Midi. Belgium and the Netherlands are both in the Schengen area.

blocks.text: Which should you pick? Choose Eurostar for the fastest trip and a station in the centre of Amsterdam. Choose Eurocity Direct when it is cheaper or the time suits you better. After Eurocity Direct, a metro or train takes you from Amsterdam Zuid to Amsterdam Centraal in about 10 minutes.

Works on some weekends change the routes: 14 to 15, 21 to 22 and 28 to 29 November and 6 to 7 December 2026. On 21 and 22 November Eurocity Direct runs to Amsterdam Centraal via Gouda and skips Schiphol. Check b-europe.com before you travel.

Bikes: Eurocity Direct takes bikes with a reservation that costs 13.90 EUR each, and space is limited.

Brussels-Midi is a busy international station with metro lines 2 and 6 and pre-metro tram lines 3 and 4. Belgian stations use two languages, so Midi and Zuid are the same place. Eurostar passengers are asked to arrive at least 20 minutes before departure. Eurocity Direct has no check-in, so find your platform and board.

Amsterdam Centraal is the main station, in the city centre, with trams, metro, buses and ferries outside. Amsterdam Zuid is south of the centre. Metro line 52 and trains connect it to Amsterdam Centraal in about 10 minutes, and metro and train connections serve Schiphol Airport.

blocks.text: Status as of 12 November 2026. This is practical information only and not legal advice. Check the official pages before you travel.

Belgium and the Netherlands are both in the Schengen area, so there is no passport control at Brussels-Midi, Amsterdam Centraal or Amsterdam Zuid. Eurostar says you do not need a passport for this trip, but customs officers carry out random spot checks, so bring an identity document.

head: Rule
Status and date

The Dutch Royal Marechaussee runs spot checks on international trains from other Schengen countries, with officers walking through the carriages to check documents. The Netherlands' temporary border controls with Belgium and Germany ended on 30 September 2026. Targeted checks continue under Mobile Security Monitoring.
Belgium has run inland entry checks since mid-2025, including on some trains at Brussels-Midi. They can happen without notice.
A valid passport or, for EU, EEA and Swiss citizens, a national ID card. Non-EU visitors should carry their passport and any visa or residence permit.

Fully operational at the external borders of the Schengen area since 10 April 2026. It records passport details and biometric data when non-EU visitors first enter. You are not asked to register again for travel inside Schengen.
Not running yet. As of August 2026 no start date has been announced. Do not pay for an authorisation now, and use only the official EU site.

sections.title: Other ways to get from Brussels to Amsterdam

blocks.text: Coach: FlixBus runs many buses a day. The fastest take about 2 hours 40 minutes, but many take longer in traffic. Fares start from about 10 EUR. In Brussels buses stop at Brussels-Nord and Brussels-Midi. In Amsterdam they use Amsterdam Sloterdijk and Amsterdam Centraal (De Ruijterkade).
Flights: not worth it. The airports are far from both centres and the train is faster overall.

Coming from another Belgian city: you can book the Eurostar and a connecting SNCB train together on eurostar.com, from hubs such as Antwerp and Liège. items: Seating: all seats are reserved. Plus and Premier seats are more spacious.
Power and Wi-Fi: free Wi-Fi and plug sockets at the seat in all three classes.

Food and drink: in Standard you can buy snacks, meals and drinks on board, and you can bring your own food. In Plus a choice of two dishes and drinks is served at your seat on London routes. Premier has a chef-designed menu.
Luggage: put larger bags in the racks at the end of the coach or above your seat. Folded pushchairs travel free in the luggage rack. Children have 1 piece of luggage plus 1 hand item.

Extra bags: on Brussels to London you can pre-book extra bags on selected trains through the Registered Luggage Service, from 35 GBP per bag, up to 85 x 85 x 36 cm. Oversized items start from 60 GBP. Check Manage your booking to see if your train is eligible.
Bikes: from 45 GBP, booked in advance. A disassembled bike up to 165 x 90 x 36 cm must be in a box or sealed bag. Eurostar also accepts fully assembled standard road bikes on the Brussels route.
Pets: pets are not allowed on trains to and from London. Guide and assistance dogs and cats may travel free if you contact Eurostar at least 24 hours before.

Accessibility: call Eurostar on +44 (0) 3432 186 186 before you travel. If you need help, arrive at least 60 minutes before departure and go to the Eurostar Assist desk. A wheelchair user fare lets you stay in your own wheelchair, and one companion can travel at a reduced rate.

blocks.text: Flights: direct flights from Brussels Airport to London take about 1 hour 5 minutes to 1 hour 20 minutes in the air. Brussels Airlines and British Airways fly direct, mostly to Heathrow. Fares from about 58 GBP appear when booked in advance, but prices vary widely by date. Add the trip to the airport (about 20 to 25 minutes by train from Brussels-Midi), security, and the trip into central London. Allow about 4 to 5 hours door to door.

Coach: FlixBus runs about 6 services a day from Brussels to London, with stops including Brussels-North, Brussels-Midi and London Victoria Coach Station. The average trip is about 8 hours 35 minutes. Fares start from about 36 GBP. Some other operators advertise a faster trip of about 6 hours 30 minutes. Fares are higher on busy dates.

Ferry plus train: Stena Line sails from Hook of Holland to Harwich. The crossing takes about 6 hours 30 minutes to 9 hours 30 minutes, and the overnight sailing leaves at 22:00 and arrives about 07:30. You need a train from Brussels to Hook of Holland and a train from Harwich to London, so this is a full day or an overnight trip. Foot passenger fares on booking sites start around 200 GBP, so check Stena Line for current prices. Dover to Calais ferries from DFDS carry vehicles only and do not take foot passengers.

Driving with Eurotunnel Le Shuttle: the crossing from Calais to Folkestone takes about 35 minutes, with up to 4 departures an hour. Day Trip and Overnight fares start from 59 GBP per car one way and need a return within 2 days. Standard fares start from 124 GBP each way for an average car. Fuel and tolls are extra. Paris Gare du Nord is at 18 Rue de Dunkerque, 75010 Paris. Eurostar departures are on the first-floor balcony in Hall 2. Follow the UK flag signs. Metro lines 4 and 5 and the RER B, D and E serve the station. A taxi stand is at the Cour des Taxis, Exit 7. The station has luggage lockers.

blocks.text: Flights: the flight takes about 1 hour 30 minutes in the air. London airports include Heathrow, Gatwick, London City, Luton and Southend. Flights land at Charles de Gaulle or Orly. Fares vary widely and low-cost fares can be close to the price of a cheap train ticket. Add the time to reach the airport, security and the trip into Paris. Allow about 5 to 7 hours door to door.
Getting to Heathrow: Heathrow Express takes about 15 minutes from Paddington. The Elizabeth line takes about 27 minutes. In Paris, RER B links Gare du Nord and Charles de Gaulle.

Coach: FlixBus runs about 6 services a day from London Victoria Coach Station to Paris Bercy. The average trip is about 8 hours. Some other coach options take up to about 10 hours. Fares start around 14 to 20 GBP but can be higher on busy dates.

Ferry plus train or coach: DFDS runs Newhaven to Dieppe. The crossing takes about 4 hours, up to 5 hours on some night sailings. You then need onward rail or coach to Paris. Check DFDS for current foot passenger fares and onward times. Dover to Calais ferries are also an option, with a coach or train on to Paris.

Driving with Eurotunnel Le Shuttle: the crossing from Folkestone to Calais takes about 35 minutes, with up to 4 departures an hour. Day Trip and Overnight fares start from 59 GBP per car one way and need a return within 2 days. Standard fares start from 124 GBP each way for an average car. Tolls on French motorways are extra. Allow about 6 to 7 hours door to door.

Paris low-emission zone: the zone covers the area inside the A86 ring road. You need a Crit'Air sticker on the windscreen. Crit'Air 0, 1 and 2 cars may enter Monday to Friday from 8:00 to 20:00. Crit'Air 3, 4 and 5 are not allowed. One report says no fines are issued until the end of 2026. Order the sticker at least 15 days before you leave.

faq.q: How long does the London to Paris train take?
faq.a: The fastest Eurostar takes 2 hours 16 minutes. The average is about 2 hours 26 minutes.

faq.q: How much does Eurostar London to Paris cost?
faq.a: Standard fares start from about 44 EUR or 39 GBP one way. Plus starts from about 70 GBP and Premier from about 245 GBP. Prices rise as the train fills.

faq.q: Where does the train arrive in Paris?
faq.a: It arrives at Paris Gare du Nord, in the 10th arrondissement. Metro lines 4 and 5 and RER B, D and E serve the station.

faq.q: How early should I check in?
faq.a: Eurostar recommends arriving 75 minutes before departure in Standard and Plus and 45 minutes in Premier. Gates close 30 minutes before departure (15 minutes in Premier).

faq.q: What are the luggage limits?
faq.a: Standard and Plus include 2 bags plus 1 small hand item. Premier includes 3 bags plus 1 hand item. Each bag can be up to 85 cm long. There is no weight limit, but you must carry the bags yourself.

faq.q: Can I take liquids on Eurostar?
faq.a: Yes. There is no 100 ml limit and no liquid volume limit on board. Some alcohol restrictions apply.

faq.q: Do I need a visa or passport?
faq.a: You need a valid passport. UK passport holders need at least 3 months left after leaving the EU and a passport less than 10 years old. Short stays of up to 90 days in any 180 days need no visa. Visitors to the UK from Europe need a UK ETA. ETIAS is not yet running.

faq.q: Can I do London to Paris as a day trip?
faq.a: Yes. With a first train around 05:40 and a last train around 20:00, a day trip is possible. Check the times for your date.

faq.q: Can children travel free?
faq.a: Children under 4 travel free if they sit on an adult's lap. Children aged 4 to 11 pay a discounted fare in Standard and Plus.

faq.q: What if the train is delayed?
faq.a: For a delay of 60 to 119 minutes you can claim 25 percent of the ticket price. For 120 minutes or more you can claim 50 percent. You can also ask for a refund or re-routing.

faq.q: Is Eurostar better than flying?
faq.a: For most people, yes. The train is centre to centre, with no long airport security queue and no 100 ml liquid rule. Flying can be cheaper on some dates.

A second class pass allows Standard only. A first class pass allows Standard or Plus. Premier is not available with a pass. Fares are indicative and seats for pass holders are limited, so book early. blocks.text: Status as of 11 November 2026. This is practical information only and not legal advice. Check the official pages named below before you travel.

Border checks: France and the Netherlands are both in the Schengen area, so there is no passport control at Gare du Nord or at Amsterdam Centraal for this trip. Eurostar says you do not need a passport to travel between France and the Netherlands, but it is worth bringing an identity document because customs carry out random spot checks. Passport control for London trains happens at Amsterdam Centraal, but it does not apply to Paris trains. You can leave the station straight away when you arrive.

head: Rule
Status and date
rows: A passport or national ID card for EU citizens. Other nationals should carry their passport and any visa or residence permit. A driving licence alone is not enough.

The temporary controls on the Dutch borders with Belgium and Germany ended on 30 September 2026. Since 1 October 2026 the Marechaussee runs expanded Mobile Security Monitoring, which allows targeted checks within 20 km of the Belgian and German borders. Checks are targeted and not systematic.

A travel-news report says France runs checks at several internal borders, including with Belgium, from 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027. Not every passenger is stopped. Check the French government site before you travel.

Fully operational at the external borders of the Schengen area since 10 April 2026. It records passport details and biometric data when non-EU visitors first enter. It replaces passport stamps. You are not asked to register again for travel inside Schengen.
Not running yet. As of August 2026 no start date has been announced. When it starts the fee will be 20 EUR. Do not pay for an authorisation now, and use only the official EU site.
Visa-free stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area. The limit covers all the countries you visit.

blocks.text: Children: every child needs their own valid travel document. Children under 12 must travel with a person aged 16 or over. Under-16s cannot travel unaccompanied on direct trains to or from the Netherlands. Travellers aged 16 and 17 can travel alone with a ticket and passport. French residents under 18 also need an AST form when travelling alone or without their parents.
Official pages to read: Eurostar travel documents, the Marechaussee page on border control, and the EU Travel Europe site for EES and ETIAS.

sections.title: Other ways to get from Paris to Amsterdam

blocks.text: Train via Brussels: take Eurostar from Paris to Brussels-Midi, which takes 1 hour 22 minutes, then a train on to Amsterdam. NS International runs the Eurocity Direct between Brussels-Midi and Amsterdam up to 16 times a day, with Saver fares from 25 EUR one way, and Eurostar runs up to 14 trains a day from Amsterdam to Brussels via Schiphol and Rotterdam. The Brussels leg takes about 2 hours. Allow time for the change. This is rarely faster than the direct train, but it can help if the direct Eurostar is sold out or too dear.

Slow rail route for pass holders: NS International lists an Interrail route from Amsterdam via Antwerp, Kortrijk, Lille Flandres and Amiens to Paris Gare du Nord. It takes about 8 hours 28 minutes and needs no seat reservation.

Flights: KLM, Air France and Transavia fly between Paris and Amsterdam Schiphol, from Charles de Gaulle and Orly. The flight takes about 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes in the air. Fares vary widely, so check the airline sites for your date. Add the time to reach the airport, security and the trip into the city. Allow about 5 to 6 hours door to door. In Paris, RER B links Gare du Nord and Charles de Gaulle.

Coach: FlixBus and BlaBlaCar Bus run about 36 services a day between them. Most leave from Paris Bercy, with others from Porte Maillot and Saint-Denis, and most arrive at Amsterdam Sloterdijk, with others at Bijlmer ArenA and Amsterdam Centraal. The fastest trip takes about 6 hours 20 minutes. Many take 7 to 8 hours. Fares start around 20 EUR and are higher on busy dates.

Parking is expensive in both cities, and most of Amsterdam's centre is closed to cars. Check low-emission zone rules for Paris and Amsterdam before you go.

faq.q: How early should I arrive?
faq.a: Eurostar recommends arriving 20 minutes before departure. Be ready to board 10 minutes before departure at Paris Gare du Nord.

faq.q: What are the luggage limits?
faq.a: Standard and Plus include 2 pieces plus 1 small hand item. Premier includes 3 pieces plus 1 hand item. Each piece can be up to 75 x 53 x 30 cm. There is no weight limit, but you must carry the bags yourself. Extra pieces cost 30 EUR each.

faq.q: Do I need a passport?
faq.a: There is no passport control between France and the Netherlands, but carry a passport or ID card because spot checks happen. EU citizens can use a national ID card.

faq.q: Can I use an Interrail or Eurail pass?
faq.a: Yes, with a seat reservation. The Interrail site lists 32 EUR in Standard and 37 EUR in Plus for Paris to Amsterdam, plus 2 EUR if you book through Interrail. Premier is not available with a pass.

faq.q: Can children travel free?
faq.a: Children under 4 travel free if they sit on an adult's lap. Children aged 4 to 11 pay a discounted fare in Standard and Plus. Under-16s cannot travel alone on direct trains to or from the Netherlands.

faq.q: What if the train is delayed?
faq.a: For a delay of 60 to 119 minutes you can claim 25 percent of the ticket price. For 120 minutes or more you can claim 50 percent. You can also ask for a refund or re-routing.

faq.q: Is the train better than flying?
faq.a: For most people, yes. The train is centre to centre, with no airport security and no liquid limit. Flying can be cheaper on some dates but takes about as long door to door.

Peak days to avoid: Friday afternoons, Sunday evenings and holiday weekends are the busiest. Cheap fares sell out first on those days.

A day trip works well in either direction. One example from autumn 2026 is a train from Budapest-Keleti at 06:30 arriving in Vienna at 09:18, and a return from Wien Hbf at 19:42 arriving in Keleti at 22:35. That leaves about ten hours in the city. Check the times for your date.

Wien Hauptbahnhof is Vienna's main station and is served by underground line U1, trams and S-Bahn trains. Many trains to Budapest also call at Wien Meidling a few minutes later. OBB lockers at Wien Hbf are multifunctional lockers, and the price is shown when you book. Standard 24-hour lockers are at Westbahnhof, Meidling and Praterstern.

Budapest-Keleti is the main arrival station for OBB and MAV trains. It is on metro lines M2 and M4. Trams 24 and 28 and several trolleybuses stop nearby. The Utascentrum ticket and service hall is open from 04:30 to 00:30. Automatic lockers are in the underpass, with small lockers about 35 x 50 x 75 cm and large lockers about 50 x 60 x 75 cm. There is no staffed left luggage office.

RegioJet trains arrive at Budapest-Deli, at the end of metro line M2. When you search on RegioJet, choose Budapest-Deli, not the general Budapest entry. Some EuroCity trains also stop at Kelenfold, which is outside the centre, so check your stop.

Vienna stops include Hauptbahnhof (Sudtiroler Platz), the Vienna International Busterminal at Erdberg, Westbahnhof and Meidling. Budapest stops include Nepliget, Kelenfold, Keleti and Mexikoi ut, and some services serve the airport. Not every trip uses every stop, so check your ticket.

Flights: flying is rarely worth it. The airports are far from both centres, and with transfers and security the trip takes longer than the train. Fare sites list fares from about 76 EUR, and prices are often higher. Check airline sites for current flights.

Pay by card where you can, and carry a little koruna for small purchases. Use bank cash machines and avoid exchange booths in the centre, which often give poor rates.

blocks.text: Prague's centre is compact and mostly walkable. One full day covers the main sights. Two nights lets you add the Jewish Quarter and a slower walk across the river. Prices below are for adults, so check each official site before you go.

items.name: Old Town Square and the Astronomical Clock
items.why: The medieval heart of the city. The clock puts on a short show on the hour, from 08:00 to 23:00. You can watch from the square for free. Go up the Old Town Hall tower for the best view of the rooftops.
items.time: 30 minutes for the square and clock, 45 minutes for the tower
items.cost: Square and clock are free. The tower is about 350 CZK.
items.getting: Metro C to Muzeum, then metro A to Staromestska. About 15 minutes.

items.name: Charles Bridge and Mala Strana
items.why: The famous stone bridge, lined with statues, leads to the quieter Lesser Town. Go early in the morning or in the evening to avoid the crowds.
items.getting: 10 minutes on foot from the Old Town Square.

items.name: Prague Castle
items.why: One of the largest castle complexes in the world. The courtyards and gardens are free. The Basic Tour covers the Old Royal Palace, St George's Basilica, St Vitus Cathedral and the Golden Lane.
items.cost: Grounds are free. The Basic Tour is about 450 CZK and the ticket is valid for 2 days. Visit Tuesday to Friday before 09:00 or after 15:00 to skip the longest queues.
items.getting: Metro A to Malostranska, then tram 22 or a walk uphill.

items.name: The Jewish Quarter
items.why: One ticket covers the synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery that are open. It is a moving and important part of the city's history.
items.cost: About 600 CZK for adults. The ticket is valid for 3 opening days. It is closed on Saturdays and Jewish holidays.
items.getting: 10 minutes on foot from the Old Town Square.

items.name: Wenceslas Square
items.why: Prague's main shopping boulevard, with the National Museum at the top. It is a good place to start or finish a walk.
items.cost: Free to walk. The museum charges admission.
items.getting: 10 minutes on foot from the station.

blocks.text: The Old Town (Stare Mesto) and New Town (Nove Mesto) are the easiest places to base yourself. Both are within walking distance of the main station and the main sights. Beds fill up on weekends and in spring, summer and December, so book early.

faq.q: How long does the train from Vienna to Prague take?
faq.a: About 4 hours 15 minutes on the direct trains. The slower regional train takes about 5 hours 10 minutes.

faq.q: How much is a train from Vienna to Prague?
faq.a: Advance tickets start from about 14.90 EUR in 2nd class on OBB, Czech Railways and RegioJet. Flexible OBB and Czech Railways tickets cost about 59 to 88 EUR.

faq.q: Is this guide also for Prague to Vienna?
faq.a: Yes. The same trains, operators and prices run in both directions. Use the Prague departure times when you travel from Prague.

faq.q: Do I need to reserve a seat?
faq.a: On OBB and Czech Railways trains a seat is optional and costs 3 EUR. RegioJet tickets always include a reserved seat. Reserve on Fridays, Sundays and in summer.

faq.q: Do I need a passport?
faq.a: Both countries are in the Schengen area, so there is no routine passport control on the train. Austria has extended temporary border controls with the Czech Republic, so carry your passport or ID card because police may ask for it.

faq.q: Which station does the train arrive at in Prague?
faq.a: Most trains arrive at Praha hlavni nadrazi, close to the centre. A few use Praha Holesovice, so check your ticket.

faq.q: Can I do Vienna to Prague as a day trip?
faq.a: You can, but it is about 8.5 hours on the train for the return. Two nights in Prague gives you a much better visit.
